title: Photos: Boston SCORES’ Annual Gala Event

content: The week of October 22, 2026 through October 29, 2026 was a very busy one for Boston SCORES, a nonprofit organization headquartered in East Boston that puts free after-school soccer programs into schools around the city where students typically wouldn’t have access to programs and activities of that kind. The week began with Celebration 2026 on Thursday October 22nd, Boston SCORES’ annual gala event, held this year at the new David Rubenstein Treehouse at Harvard. More than 300 people attended and over $320,000 was raised towards the work the organization does. Then on Saturday October 24th and Sunday October 25th, Boston SCORES played host to the first round of the 2026 Mayor’s Cup, a citywide soccer tournament bringing together soccer programs from around the city to compete in a weekend long event. 3 years ago Boston SCORES was able to raise $17 million dollars through an ambitious capital campaign and was able to create their own field and facilities in East Boston where they are located. Along with the creation of this community space, the organization was able to bring the first community focused soccer league to East Boston, aptly named East Boston FC, with one of the EBFC teams even taking home the trophy at the end of the weekend. The week concluded with the organization’s first Open Mic poetry night of the year. As part of their full scope approach to youth development, every student on a Boston SCORES afterschool or community team also participates in an evolving and impactful enrichment curriculum, with elementary aged students using poetry as the vessel for that development. Students created and performed their own original works, local artists presented students with pieces based on their poetry, and community members were able to see the enrichment side of the program in action.
